arxiv-2105-08645.title: CoTexT: Multi-task Learning with Code-Text Transformer
arxiv-2105-08645.creator: Long Phan, Hieu Tran, Daniel Le, Hieu Nguyen, James Anibal, Alec Peltekian, Yanfang Ye
arxiv-2105-08645.description: Abstract We present CoTexT, a pre-trained, transformer-based encoder-decoder model that learns the representative context between natural language (NL) and programming language (PL). Using self-supervision, CoTexT is pre-trained on large programming language corpora to learn a general understanding of language and code. CoTexT supports downstream NL-PL tasks such as code summarizing/documentation, code generation, defect detection, and code debugging.

arxiv-2211-02117.title: Hydrodynamics of plastic deformations in electronic crystals
arxiv-2211-02117.creator: Jay Armas, Erik van Heumen, Akash Jain, Ruben Lier
arxiv-2211-02117.description: Abstract We construct a new hydrodynamic framework describing plastic deformations in electronic crystals. The framework accounts for pinning, phase, and momentum relaxation effects due to translational disorder, diffusion due to the presence of interstitials and vacancies, and strain relaxation due to plasticity and dislocations.

arxiv-2312-12806.title: MedBench: A Large-Scale Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Medical Large Language Models
arxiv-2312-12806.creator: Yan Cai, Linlin Wang, Ye Wang, Gerard de Melo, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Liang He
arxiv-2312-12806.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yan Cai, Linlin Wang, Ye Wang, Gerard de Melo, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Liang He. The emergence of various medical large language models (LLMs) in the medical domain has highlighted the need for unified evaluation standards, as manual evaluation of LLMs proves to be time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this issue, we introduce MedBench, a comprehensive benchmark for the Chinese medical domain, comprising 40,041 questions sourced from authentic examination exercises and medical reports of diverse branches of medicine.

arxiv-2403-11806.title: Fluid Antenna for Mobile Edge Computing Thanks: Yiping Zuo, Biyun Sheng, Chen Dai, and Fu Xiao are with the School of Computer Science, Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Nanjing 210023, China (Email: zuoyiping@njupt.edu.cn, biyunsheng@njupt.edu.cn, daichen@njupt.edu.cn, xiaof@njupt
arxiv-2403-11806.creator: Yiping Zuo, Jiajia Guo, Biyun Sheng, Chen Dai
arxiv-2403-11806.description: Abstract In the evolving environment of mobile edge computing (MEC), optimizing system performance to meet the growing demand for low-latency computing services is a top priority. Integrating fluidic antenna (FA) technology into MEC networks provides a new approach to address this challenge.

arxiv-2503-21310.title: The evolving boundary of green technology
arxiv-2503-21310.creator: Nicolò Barbieri, Kerstin Hötte, Peter Persoon
arxiv-2503-21310.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicolò Barbieri, Kerstin Hötte, Peter Persoon. Green patent indicators are widely used to track technological progress, assess climate and innovation policies, and identify emerging technological opportunities. Yet these indicators depend on classification systems that evolve over time and shape which inventions become visible.

pmc-10579866.title: A rare, likely pathogenic variant causing Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy in three-generation females of an African-American family
pmc-10579866.creator: Yanjun Chen, Elizabeth R Kellom
pmc-10579866.description: PurposeWe report a rare, likely pathogenic variant gene causing Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) in three-generation female members of an African-American family.ObservationsThe granddaughter and mother presented with a subacute, painless visual loss in both eyes at age 10 and 42 years to legal blindness. The maternal grandmother presented with a gradual onset of moderate visual loss at age 60.

pmc-10673087.title: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography-Based Investigation of the Frequency and Pattern of Radix Entomolaris in the Saudi Arabian Population
pmc-10673087.creator: Muhammad Qasim Javed, Swati Srivastava, Badi Baen Rashed Alotaibi, Usman Anwer Bhatti, Ayman M Abulhamael, Syed Rashid Habib, Bruno Chrcanovic, Romica Cergan, Adrian Costache, Mihai Dumitru
pmc-10673087.description: Background and Objectives: An understanding of the anatomical complexity of teeth is a significant factor for a successful endodontic treatment outcome. The aim of this study was to explore the frequency and pattern of distribution of radix entomolaris (RE) in mandibular first molars (MFMs) of a Saudi Arabian subpopulation using CBCT scans.

pmc-10710573.title: 10005-ANGI-1 REGULATION OF ALTERNATIVE ANGIOGENIC FACTORS IN BEVACIZUMAB THERAPY FOR GLIOBLASTOMA
pmc-10710573.creator: Taketo Ezaki, Toshihide Tanaka, Ryota Tamura, Yohei Yamamoto, Jun Takei, Yukina Morimoto, Ryotaro Imai, Yuki Kuranari, Yasuharu Akasaki, Yuichi Murayama, Keisuke Miyake, Hikaru Sasaki
pmc-10710573.description: The elucidation of the mechanism of action and resistance is imperative to overcome resistance to Bev and develop a more effective therapy. This study aims to investigate the status and change of alternative angiogenic factors regarding Bev usage using human specimens.

pmc-11340740.title: Yellow fever vaccine coverage and associated factors among under-five children in Kenya: Data from Kenyan Demographic and Health Survey 2022
pmc-11340740.creator: Mohammed Seid Ali, Enyew Getaneh Mekonen
pmc-11340740.description: Yellow fever is a vaccine preventable hemorrhagic disease that leads to morbidity and mortality in the affected individuals. The only options for preventing and controlling its spread are through vaccination. Therefore, this study was conducted to estimate yellow fever vaccination coverage and associated factors among under-five children in Kenya.

pmc-12853386.title: Scientific Validation of "Clinically Proven" Claims: Compliance Focused and Global Regulatory Insights
pmc-12853386.creator: Maheshvari N Patel, Nayan Patel
pmc-12853386.description: The designation “clinically proven” represents a product's validation through scientifically rigorous, ethically sound, and regulatory-compliant clinical research. Establishing such a claim demands a systematic continuum from preclinical evaluations to well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs), multicentric validations, and real-world evidence studies that collectively demonstrate safety, efficacy, and reproducibility.

pmc-12912328.title: Prior-night sleep predicts next-day symptoms over ten days among military personnel with sleep problems
pmc-12912328.creator: Emerson M Wickwire, Jacob Collen, Vincent F Capaldi, Zhiwei Zhao, Scott G Williams, Connie L Thomas, Samson Z Assefa, Jennifer S Albrecht, Shuo Chen
pmc-12912328.description: This study employed remote monitoring/ecological momentary assessment methods to test the hypothesis that prior-night sleep is associated with next-day symptoms. Military personnel with sleep problems (N = 270) completed daily sleep diaries and twice-daily symptom surveys via smartphone and wore a commercial wearable for ten days.

pmc-13408101.title: Advances in the Interpretation of the Electrocardiogram by Artificial Intelligence
pmc-13408101.creator: S. Suave Lobodzinski, Ryszard Piotrowicz
pmc-13408101.description: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is essential for cardiovascular diagnosis but limited by inter-observer variability, low sensitivity for subclinical disease, and labor-intensive telemonitoring analysis. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, addresses these constraints by extracting high-dimensional patterns that correlate with arrhythmias, structural abnormalities, and systemic conditions.

pmc-13615417.title: Divergent Obesity Classification Between the Edmonton Obesity Staging System and the Lancet Commission Model
pmc-13615417.creator: Tobias Hagemann, Arya M Sharma, Matthias Blüher, Anne Hoffmann
pmc-13615417.description: ObjectiveBMI alone does not capture obesity‐related health heterogeneity. The Edmonton Obesity Staging System (EOSS) grades obesity severity based on comorbidities and functional impairment, whereas the Lancet Commission Diagnostic Model for Obesity (DMO) distinguishes preclinical from clinical obesity based on organ dysfunction. We compared classification patterns and concordance across both obesity frameworks in a large population‐based cohort.
